chapter: Family background and the Tulsa music scene
title: His mother as manicurist and band booker in Sapulpa
summary: His mother met bands as a barbershop manicurist and booked bands at a riverbank dance hall.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: And you were telling me, at one point, your mother booked bands.
That was in Sepulpa, Oklahoma, that was just out from Tulsa. Sepulpa and Sand Springs, they were all close together in West Tulsa.
That was later, and that was when you were how old?
Oh, I imagine I was about nine, I guess.
When you were living in Tulsa.
Yeah, we'd been to Kansas City and come back to Tulsa. And --
How did your mother happen to get into band booking?

Well, she was a manicurist in the barber shop. And invariably, she met all of the bands that came through because they would come through for manicures and things like that. Anything to look good, the haircuts and the manicures. And I met a lot of them that way besides going into these rehearsals. And I met Louis Armstrong getting a manicure,

when he had the Hot Five.

And behind meeting all these musicians, someone told her, say, "Nola," say, "You and your getup," they say, "Why don't you get all these musicians, you know, this one dance hall, why don't you start booking bands, you know, see if you can get a band down here for you," you know?

So she started inquiring and finally she did. And they had a sort of a frame dance hall. No enclosure at all, just looked like a frame of a house, you know, with a dance floor. And it was right on the bank of the Arkansas River.

Now, what bands there were, that she booked in there, I can't recall any of them. But she said she had Alphonso Trent there once, and she had Effie Jackson there once. But I don't recall who was there, because I never did go down, you know, to the river because I was living with my grandmother.
